definitions.explanation: A divine being worshipped in religion.
A sacred spirit in Shinto belief.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{神|かみ}に{祈|いの}った。
examples.english: I prayed to the gods at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {神様|かみさま}、どうかお{守|まも}りください。
{日本|にほん}には{八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ}がいる。
examples.english: In Japan, there are eight million gods.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}のあらゆるものに{神|かみ}が{宿|やど}ると{信|しん}じられている。
examples.english: It is believed that spirits dwell in all things in nature.

notes:
{神|かみ} means god, deity, or spirit. In Japanese culture, this concept differs significantly from Western monotheism.

SHINTO CONCEPT:
In Shinto, {神|かみ} ({八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ} = 'eight million gods') refers to spirits inhabiting nature, ancestors, and sacred places. Almost anything can be considered a {神|かみ}.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {神様|かみさま}: god (honorific form)
- {神社|じんじゃ}: Shinto shrine
- {神道|しんとう}: Shinto
- {神話|しんわ}: mythology
- {神棚|かみだな}: household Shinto altar

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {神|かみ}に{祈|いの}る: to pray to god(s)
- {神頼|かみだの}み: relying on divine help
- {神|かみ}{業|わざ}: divine work, miraculous skill

MODERN SLANG:
{神|かみ} is used colloquially to mean 'amazing' or 'godlike': この{曲|きょく}{神|かみ}! (This song is amazing!)
